guide.what: A reflexive or pronominal verb is a verb used with a pronoun (me, te, se, nos) that matches the subject. In the dictionary it ends in -se: levantarse, irse, quejarse. Sometimes the action falls back on the subject ('I wash myself'), but often the 'se' just changes or colors the meaning.

rules.d: In a true reflexive, the person who does the action also receives it: 'lavo el carro' (I wash the car) vs 'me lavo' (I wash myself). English often drops 'myself', but Spanish needs the pronoun.
rules.ex: Baño al bebé y después me baño yo.
rules.exEn: I bathe the baby and then I take a shower.

rules.t: The pronouns: me, te, se, nos, se
rules.d: The pronoun always matches the subject. Full present of levantarse: yo me levanto, tú te levantas, vos te levantás, él/ella/usted se levanta, nosotros nos levantamos, ustedes se levantan, ellos/ellas se levantan. Spain also uses vosotros os levantáis.
rules.ex: Nosotros nos levantamos temprano, pero ustedes se levantan tarde.
rules.exEn: We get up early, but you all get up late.

rules.d: Put it before a conjugated verb (me levanto, no me levanto). Attach it to the end of an infinitive, a gerund (-ando/-iendo) or an affirmative command, adding an accent when needed: levántate, estoy duchándome. With 'voy a' or 'estoy' you can choose: voy a levantarme = me voy a levantar.
rules.ex: Me estoy duchando. / Estoy duchándome. ¡Levántate ya!
rules.exEn: I'm taking a shower. Get up now!

rules.t: Body parts and clothes take 'el/la', not 'mi'
rules.d: The pronoun already shows whose body it is, so use the article: me lavo las manos, me pongo la camisa, se rompió la pierna. 'Mis manos' here sounds odd.
rules.ex: Me lavo las manos y me quito los zapatos.
rules.exEn: I wash my hands and take off my shoes.

rules.t: Not every 'se' means 'myself': the main types
rules.d: Daily routine (me levanto, me visto). Meaning changes: ir/irse (go/leave), dormir/dormirse (sleep/fall asleep), llevar/llevarse bien (carry/get along), quedar/quedarse (meet/stay), parecer/parecerse (seem/look like), acordar/acordarse (agree/remember), negar/negarse (deny/refuse). Always pronominal: me quejo, me arrepiento, me atrevo, me doy cuenta. Emotions: me preocupo, me aburro. Movement and position: me siento, me mudo. Emphatic: se comió toda la pizza, me tomé un café. Many of these need a preposition: acordarse de, casarse con, enamorarse de, atreverse a, fijarse en.
rules.ex: Me fui temprano porque me dormí en la reunión.
rules.exEn: I left early because I fell asleep in the meeting.

rules.d: With a plural subject, nos/se can mean 'each other': nos conocimos, se abrazaron, nos escribimos. Add 'el uno al otro' only if it's unclear.
rules.ex: Nos conocimos en 2019 y nos escribimos todos los días.
rules.exEn: We met in 2019 and we text each other every day.

rules.d: To show something happened by accident, use se + me/te/le/nos/les + verb. The thing is the subject, so the verb agrees with it: se me cayó el vaso, se me cayeron los platos. Common with olvidar, caer, romper, perder, quedar, acabar.
rules.ex: Se me olvidó el celular y se le perdieron las llaves a Juan.
rules.exEn: I forgot my phone and Juan lost his keys.

rules.t: 'Se' verbs for becoming (to get / to become)
rules.d: Spanish has no single word for 'get/become'. ponerse + adjective = quick change (ponerse nervioso, rojo). hacerse = by effort (hacerse rico, médico). volverse = deep change (volverse loco). quedarse = result after something (quedarse dormido, sorprendido). convertirse en + noun = turn into.
rules.ex: Se puso nervioso, se quedó callado y casi se vuelve loco.
rules.exEn: He got nervous, went quiet and almost went crazy.

rules.d: The pronoun goes before 'haber': me he levantado, se han ido, nos habíamos acostado. In Panama and most of Latin America the simple past is preferred for today's actions: 'Hoy me levanté tarde' (Spain: 'Hoy me he levantado tarde').
rules.ex: Hoy me levanté tarde, pero ya me he duchado.
rules.exEn: Today I got up late, but I've already showered.

mistakes.why: Without 'me' it means 'I lift (something)'; 'get up' needs the pronoun.
With body parts and clothes, use the article; 'me' already shows whose.

mistakes.right: Me voy a duchar. / Voy a ducharme.
mistakes.why: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or attached to the infinitive, never between.

mistakes.right: No me acuerdo de tu nombre.
mistakes.why: acordarse needs 'de' (or say 'No recuerdo tu nombre').

mistakes.wrong: Se casó a un panameño y se enamoró con él.
mistakes.right: Se casó con un panameño y se enamoró de él.
mistakes.why: Fixed prepositions: casarse con, enamorarse de.
'caer' can't take an object; use accidental se with the phone as subject.

items.use: ir = go (to a place); irse = leave (the place you are in). Irregular: me voy, te vas, se fue, nos fuimos.
items.ex: Ya me voy, nos vemos mañana.
items.exEn: I'm leaving now, see you tomorrow.

items.use: quedar = arrange to meet / be located / fit; quedarse = stay somewhere. Regular -ar verb.
items.ex: Este fin de semana me quedo en casa.
items.exEn: This weekend I'm staying home.

items.use: llamar = call (phone, shout); llamarse = to be named. Regular. Say 'Me llamo Ana', not 'Mi nombre es llamo'.
items.ex: Me llamo Ana, ¿y tú cómo te llamas?
items.exEn: My name is Ana, and what's your name?

items.use: sentir + noun = feel/sense something (sentir frío); sentirse + adjective/adverb = feel (bien, cansado). Irregular e→ie and e→i: me siento, se sintió.
items.ex: Hoy me siento un poco cansada.
items.exEn: Today I feel a little tired.

items.use: Fixed expression: always with se and 'de' before a noun or a 'que' clause. 'dar' is irregular: me doy cuenta, me di cuenta. Not 'realizar' (that means carry out).
items.ex: No me di cuenta de que era tan tarde.
items.exEn: I didn't realize it was so late.

items.use: poner = put something somewhere; ponerse = put on clothes, shoes, makeup. Irregular: me pongo, se puso. Use the article, not 'mi': me pongo la camisa.
items.ex: Ponte la chaqueta, que está lloviendo.
items.exEn: Put on your jacket, it's raining.

items.use: For quick, temporary changes of mood, color or health: ponerse nervioso, rojo, triste, enfermo. Irregular: se puso, se pone.
items.ex: Se puso muy nerviosa antes del examen.
items.exEn: She got very nervous before the exam.

items.use: acordar = agree on; acordarse de = remember. Always 'de' before the thing. o→ue: me acuerdo, te acuerdas.
items.ex: ¿Te acuerdas de mi hermano Carlos?
items.exEn: Do you remember my brother Carlos?

items.use: preocupar = worry someone else (Me preocupa la salud); preocuparse por = be worried about. Regular.
items.ex: No te preocupes, todo va a salir bien.
items.exEn: Don't worry, everything will be fine.

items.use: levantar = lift something; levantarse = get up (out of bed or a chair). Regular: me levanto, te levantas.
items.ex: Me levanto a las seis todos los días.
items.exEn: I get up at six every day.

items.use: casar = to marry (a couple, as a priest or judge does); casarse con = get married to. Use 'con', never 'a'. Regular.
items.ex: Mi prima se casó con un panameño.
items.exEn: My cousin married a Panamanian.

items.use: encontrar = find; encontrarse con = run into someone; encontrarse + adjective = be/feel (formal). o→ue: me encuentro.
items.ex: Me encontré con Luis en el supermercado.
items.exEn: I ran into Luis at the supermarket.

items.en: to do for a living; to devote oneself
items.use: dedicar = dedicate something; dedicarse a = work as / spend your time on. c→qu before e: me dediqué.
items.ex: ¿A qué te dedicas? —Soy enfermera.
items.exEn: What do you do for a living? —I'm a nurse.

items.use: Almost always pronominal. Use 'de' before the news. Regular. Very common for hearing news or gossip.
items.ex: Me enteré de la noticia por la radio.
items.exEn: I found out about the news on the radio.

items.use: Three options: olvidé las llaves / me olvidé de las llaves / se me olvidaron las llaves. The last one ('it slipped my mind') is the most common in speech. Regular.
items.ex: Se me olvidaron las llaves en la oficina.
items.exEn: I forgot my keys at the office.

items.use: volver = return; volverse + adjective = become, often a lasting or negative change (loco, serio, famoso). o→ue: se vuelve.
items.ex: Se volvió muy serio después del accidente.
items.exEn: He became very serious after the accident.

items.use: hacer = do/make; hacerse + noun/adjective = become by choice or effort (rico, médico, famoso). Also 'se hace tarde' = it's getting late. Irregular: se hizo.
items.ex: Se hizo médico a los treinta años.
items.exEn: He became a doctor at thirty.

items.use: sentar = seat someone; sentarse = sit down. e→ie: me siento (same form as 'I feel' from sentirse; context tells you which).
items.ex: Siéntese, por favor, el doctor ya viene.
items.exEn: Please sit down, the doctor is coming.

items.use: despertar = wake someone else up; despertarse = wake up yourself. e→ie: me despierto.
items.ex: Me despierto antes de que suene la alarma.
items.exEn: I wake up before the alarm goes off.

items.en: to go to bed, to lie down
items.use: acostar = put someone to bed; acostarse = go to bed. o→ue: me acuesto, te acuestas.
items.ex: Los niños se acuestan a las ocho.
items.exEn: The kids go to bed at eight.

items.en: to shower, to bathe; to swim
items.use: bañar = bathe someone (a baby, a dog); bañarse = take a shower/bath, or swim in the sea or a pool. Regular.
items.ex: Me baño todas las mañanas antes del trabajo.
items.exEn: I shower every morning before work.
items.latam: In Panama and most of Latin America 'bañarse' is the everyday word for showering. In Spain 'bañarse' means taking a bath or swimming; for a shower they say 'ducharse'.

items.use: Regular. Clear and understood everywhere, but in Latin America 'bañarse' is more common in conversation.
items.ex: Me ducho con agua fría porque hace calor.
items.exEn: I shower with cold water because it's hot.
items.latam: Common in Spain; in Panama people mostly say 'bañarse'.

items.use: vestir = dress someone; vestirse = get dressed. e→i: me visto, se vistió.
items.ex: Me visto rápido y salgo para la oficina.
items.exEn: I get dressed quickly and leave for the office.

items.use: lavar = wash something (el carro); lavarse = wash part of yourself. Use the article: me lavo las manos, not 'mis manos'. Regular.
items.ex: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
items.exEn: Wash your hands before eating.

items.use: dormir = sleep; dormirse = fall asleep (the moment). Also 'oversleep' in context. o→ue and o→u: me duermo, se durmió.
items.ex: Me dormí viendo la película.
items.exEn: I fell asleep watching the movie.

items.use: Always used with se. Use 'de' before what you complain about. Regular.
items.ex: Mi jefe siempre se queja del tráfico.
items.exEn: My boss always complains about the traffic.

items.use: enamorar = make someone fall in love; enamorarse de = fall in love with. Use 'de', not 'con'. Regular.
items.ex: Se enamoró de ella en la universidad.
items.exEn: He fell in love with her at university.

items.en: to make a mistake, to be wrong
items.use: Almost always with se. 'equivocarse de' = get the wrong (number, day). c→qu before e: me equivoqué.
items.ex: Perdón, me equivoqué de número.
items.exEn: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.

items.use: enojar = make someone angry; enojarse con alguien = get angry at someone. Regular.
items.ex: Se enojó conmigo porque llegué tarde.
items.exEn: She got mad at me because I arrived late.
items.latam: Spain says 'enfadarse'. In Panama you also hear 'ponerse bravo'.

items.use: divertir = amuse others; divertirse = have a good time. e→ie and e→i: me divierto, se divirtieron.
items.ex: ¡Que te diviertas en la fiesta!
items.exEn: Have fun at the party!

items.use: Usually used with se. 'reírse de' = laugh at. e→i with accents: me río, te ríes, se rio (no accent on 'rio').
items.ex: Nos reímos mucho con sus chistes.
items.exEn: We laughed a lot at his jokes.

items.use: morir = die (neutral, news); morirse = die (more personal) and 'morirse de' = be dying of (hunger, laughter). o→ue and o→u: me muero, se murió.
items.ex: Me muero de hambre, ¿comemos?
items.exEn: I'm starving, shall we eat?

items.use: llevar = carry, take, wear; llevarse bien/mal con = get along with someone. Regular.
items.ex: Me llevo muy bien con mi suegra.
items.exEn: I get along really well with my mother-in-law.

items.use: parecer = seem; parecerse a = look like someone. c→zc in yo: me parezco.
items.ex: Te pareces mucho a tu mamá.
items.exEn: You look a lot like your mom.

items.en: to meet (each other); to know each other
items.use: conocer = know / meet someone; conocerse = meet each other (first time) or know each other. c→zc: conozco.
items.ex: Nos conocimos en la universidad.
items.exEn: We met at university.

items.en: to see each other, to meet up
items.use: ver = see; verse = see each other. Also 'verse + adjective' = look (Te ves bien). Irregular: nos vimos.
items.ex: Nos vemos el viernes en el café.
items.exEn: See you Friday at the café.

items.use: tratar = treat / try; se trata de = it's about / it's a matter of. Only in the form 'se trata de', with no person as subject.
items.ex: No se trata de dinero, se trata de respeto.
items.exEn: It's not about money, it's about respect.

items.use: Same meaning as imaginar, but with se it sounds more natural in conversation. 'Me imagino que...' = I suppose that... Regular.
items.ex: Me imagino que estás cansado del viaje.
items.exEn: I imagine you're tired from the trip.

items.use: cansar = tire someone out; cansarse = get tired; 'cansarse de' = get tired of. Regular.
items.ex: Me canso mucho cuando subo las escaleras.
items.exEn: I get very tired when I climb the stairs.

items.use: aburrir = bore someone; aburrirse = get bored. 'Estoy aburrido' = I'm bored; 'soy aburrido' = I'm boring. Regular.
items.ex: Los niños se aburren en los viajes largos.
items.exEn: Kids get bored on long trips.

items.use: alegrar = make someone happy; alegrarse de = be glad. 'Me alegro de que' + subjunctive. Regular.
items.ex: Me alegro de que estés mejor.
items.exEn: I'm glad you're feeling better.

items.use: comer = eat; comerse = eat a specific, whole amount. Needs a concrete object: se comió la pizza (not 'se comió pizza').
items.ex: Se comió toda la pizza él solo.
items.exEn: He ate the whole pizza by himself.

items.use: Accidental se: se + me/te/le + caer. The thing dropped is the subject: se me cayó el vaso, se me cayeron los platos. Irregular: se cayó.
items.ex: Se me cayó el celular en la calle.
items.exEn: I dropped my phone in the street.

items.use: caer = fall (rain, prices); caerse = fall over, trip and fall. Irregular: me caigo, se cayó.
items.ex: Mi abuela se cayó en el baño.
items.exEn: My grandmother fell in the bathroom.

items.use: quitar = remove something; quitarse = take off clothes, shoes, glasses. Use the article: me quito los zapatos. Regular.
items.ex: Quítate los zapatos antes de entrar.
items.exEn: Take off your shoes before coming in.

items.use: Regular. Use the article: me cepillo los dientes, not 'mis dientes'.
items.ex: Me cepillo los dientes después de cada comida.
items.exEn: I brush my teeth after every meal.
items.latam: Very common in Latin America; in Spain 'lavarse los dientes' is more usual.

items.use: mudar = change (skin, feathers); mudarse = move to a new home. Not 'moverse' (that is physical movement). Regular.
items.ex: Nos mudamos a Panamá el año pasado.
items.exEn: We moved to Panama last year.

items.use: fijar = fix, set (a date); fijarse en = notice / look carefully at. 'Fíjate' = look / listen to this. Regular.
items.ex: Fíjate en el precio antes de comprar.
items.exEn: Look at the price before buying.

items.use: Always with se. 'atreverse a' + infinitive. Regular.
items.ex: No me atrevo a decirle la verdad.
items.exEn: I don't dare tell him the truth.

items.use: convertir = convert something; convertirse en + noun = turn into. e→ie and e→i: se convierte, se convirtió.
items.ex: El pueblo se convirtió en una ciudad.
items.exEn: The town turned into a city.

items.use: quedarse con = keep something / take it for yourself. Common when shopping: 'Me quedo con esta' = I'll take this one.
items.ex: Me quedo con la camisa azul, gracias.
items.exEn: I'll take the blue shirt, thanks.

items.en: to end up, to be left (in a state)
items.use: For the result of a change: quedarse dormido (fall asleep), callado (go quiet), sorprendido, sin dinero.
items.ex: Me quedé dormido y llegué tarde.
items.exEn: I overslept and arrived late.

items.use: ponerse a + infinitive = suddenly start an action. Irregular: se puso a.
items.ex: Cuando oyó la noticia, se puso a llorar.
items.exEn: When she heard the news, she started to cry.

items.en: to take away, to take with you
items.use: llevar = carry/take; llevarse = take something away for good. Also 'llevarse una sorpresa' = get a surprise. Regular.
items.ex: ¿Para comer aquí o para llevar? —Me lo llevo.
items.exEn: For here or to go? —I'll take it with me.

items.use: tomar = drink/take; tomarse = drink a whole, specific thing, or take time off: tomarse un café, tomarse el día libre. Regular.
items.ex: Me tomé un café antes de la reunión.
items.exEn: I had a coffee before the meeting.

items.en: to get lost; to miss (an event)
items.use: perder = lose / miss (a bus); perderse = get lost, or miss out on something fun. e→ie: me pierdo.
items.ex: Nos perdimos en el Casco Viejo.
items.exEn: We got lost in Casco Viejo.

items.use: Accidental se: se me perdió la cartera = I lost my wallet (it wasn't my fault). The lost thing is the subject.
items.ex: Se me perdieron las gafas otra vez.
items.exEn: I lost my glasses again.
items.latam: In Panama you'll also hear 'los lentes' for glasses.

items.use: Accidental se: se me rompió = it broke on me. 'Rompí el vaso' sounds like you did it on purpose. Irregular participle: roto.
items.ex: Perdón, se me rompió el vaso.
items.exEn: Sorry, the glass broke (I broke it by accident).

items.use: Accidental se: se me quedó = I left it behind without meaning to. The thing left is the subject.
items.ex: Se me quedó la cartera en el carro.
items.exEn: I left my wallet in the car.

items.en: to occur to someone, to have an idea
items.use: ocurrir = happen; se me ocurre / se me ocurrió = an idea comes to me. The idea is the subject.
items.ex: Se me ocurrió una idea genial.
items.exEn: I had a great idea.

items.use: Accidental se: se me acabó el saldo = I ran out of phone credit. Also 'se acabó' = it's over / it ran out.
items.ex: Se me acabó la batería del celular.
items.exEn: My phone battery died.

items.use: despedir = fire (from a job) or see someone off; despedirse de = say goodbye. e→i: me despido, se despidió.
items.ex: Me despedí de todos y me fui a casa.
items.exEn: I said goodbye to everyone and went home.

items.use: negar = deny; negarse a + infinitive = refuse to. e→ie: me niego; g→gu: me negué.
items.ex: El testigo se negó a hablar.
items.exEn: The witness refused to talk.

items.use: Always with se. 'de' before what you regret. e→ie and e→i: me arrepiento, se arrepintió.
items.ex: No me arrepiento de nada.
items.exEn: I don't regret anything.

items.use: burlar = get around (security, a law); burlarse de = mock someone. Regular.
items.ex: No te burles de tu hermano.
items.exEn: Don't make fun of your brother.

items.use: portar = carry (formal: portar armas); portarse bien/mal = behave. Regular.
items.ex: Si te portas bien, vamos al parque.
items.exEn: If you behave, we'll go to the park.

items.use: relajar = relax something (muscles); relajarse = relax yourself. Regular.
items.ex: Los domingos me relajo en la playa.
items.exEn: On Sundays I relax at the beach.

items.use: calmar = calm someone; calmarse = calm down. 'Cálmate' is common but can sound bossy; 'tranquilo/a' is softer.
items.ex: Cálmate, no es para tanto.
items.exEn: Calm down, it's not a big deal.

items.use: apurar = rush someone / finish a drink; apurarse = hurry. Regular.
items.ex: Apúrate, que el bus ya viene.
items.exEn: Hurry up, the bus is coming.
items.latam: Standard in Panama and Latin America. Spain says 'darse prisa' (¡Date prisa!).

items.en: to be quiet, to shut up
items.use: callar = silence someone or keep something quiet; callarse = stop talking. '¡Cállate!' is rude; 'silencio, por favor' is polite.
items.ex: Cuando entró el profesor, todos se callaron.
items.exEn: When the teacher came in, everyone went quiet.

items.use: cuidar = look after someone; cuidarse = look after yourself. 'Cuídate' is a common goodbye. Regular.
items.ex: Cuídate mucho y escríbeme.
items.exEn: Take good care of yourself and write to me.

items.use: preparar = prepare something (food); prepararse para = get yourself ready. Regular.
items.ex: Me estoy preparando para el DELE.
items.exEn: I'm preparing for the DELE.

items.en: to get ready, to dress up
items.use: arreglar = fix; arreglarse = get dressed up / ready to go out. 'arreglárselas' = manage. Regular.
items.ex: Me arreglo en diez minutos y salimos.
items.exEn: I'll get ready in ten minutes and we'll go.

items.use: peinar = comb someone else's hair; peinarse = do your own hair. Regular.
items.ex: Mi hijo nunca se peina por la mañana.
items.exEn: My son never combs his hair in the morning.

items.use: afeitar = shave someone; afeitarse = shave yourself. Regular. Use the article: me afeito la barba.
items.ex: Mi papá se afeita todas las mañanas.
items.exEn: My dad shaves every morning.
items.latam: In Mexico and parts of Central America you'll also hear 'rasurarse'.

items.use: maquillar = do someone's makeup; maquillarse = do your own. Regular.
items.ex: Se maquilla en el bus camino al trabajo.
items.exEn: She does her makeup on the bus to work.

items.use: secar = dry something; secarse = dry yourself. c→qu before e: me sequé. Use the article: me seco el pelo.
items.ex: Sécate bien el pelo antes de salir.
items.exEn: Dry your hair well before going out.

items.use: cambiar = change something; cambiarse = change clothes; cambiarse de casa = move house. Regular.
items.ex: Me cambio y te alcanzo en cinco minutos.
items.exEn: I'll get changed and catch up with you in five minutes.

items.use: probar = taste / try; probarse = try on clothes. o→ue: me pruebo.
items.ex: ¿Me puedo probar estos zapatos?
items.exEn: Can I try on these shoes?

items.use: mirar = look at; mirarse = look at yourself, or at each other. Regular.
items.ex: Se mira en el espejo antes de salir.
items.exEn: She looks at herself in the mirror before leaving.

items.en: to cut oneself; to get a haircut
items.use: cortar = cut; cortarse = cut yourself; cortarse el pelo = get your hair cut (even if a barber does it). Regular.
items.ex: Ayer me corté el pelo en la barbería.
items.exEn: Yesterday I got a haircut at the barbershop.

items.use: abrazar = hug someone; abrazarse = hug each other. z→c before e: nos abrazamos, me abracé.
items.ex: Los hermanos se abrazaron en el aeropuerto.
items.exEn: The brothers hugged at the airport.

items.use: besar = kiss someone; besarse = kiss each other. Regular.
items.ex: Al final de la boda, los novios se besaron.
items.exEn: At the end of the wedding, the couple kissed.

items.use: escribir = write; escribirse = write to each other / text each other. Irregular participle: escrito.
items.ex: Nos escribimos por WhatsApp todos los días.
items.exEn: We text each other on WhatsApp every day.

items.use: hablar = speak; hablarse = speak to each other. Often negative: 'no se hablan' = they're not on speaking terms.
items.ex: Mis tíos ya no se hablan.
items.exEn: My aunt and uncle don't speak to each other anymore.

items.use: ayudar = help; ayudarse = help each other. Regular.
items.ex: En mi familia siempre nos ayudamos.
items.exEn: In my family we always help each other.

items.use: pelear = fight; pelearse con = fall out / argue with someone. Regular.
items.ex: Se pelearon por una tontería.
items.exEn: They had a fight over something silly.

items.en: to get together, to hang out (with)
items.use: juntar = put together / collect; juntarse = meet up; juntarse con = hang out with. Regular.
items.ex: Los sábados nos juntamos a ver el fútbol.
items.exEn: On Saturdays we get together to watch soccer.

items.use: reunir = gather things or people; reunirse con = have a meeting with. Accent: me reúno, se reúnen.
items.ex: Mañana me reúno con el cliente.
items.exEn: Tomorrow I'm meeting with the client.

items.en: to get along, to understand each other
items.use: entender = understand; entenderse con = get along / communicate well with. e→ie: nos entendemos.
items.ex: Mi jefe y yo nos entendemos muy bien.
items.exEn: My boss and I get along very well.

items.use: separar = separate things; separarse = split up (a couple) or move apart. Regular.
items.ex: Mis papás se separaron cuando yo era niño.
items.exEn: My parents split up when I was a kid.

items.use: Almost always with se: divorciarse de alguien. Regular.
items.ex: Se divorció de su esposo hace dos años.
items.exEn: She divorced her husband two years ago.

items.use: graduar = adjust (a level); graduarse = graduate. Accent: me gradúo, se gradúa. 'graduarse de' + degree/school.
items.ex: Mi hija se graduó de la universidad en diciembre.
items.exEn: My daughter graduated from university in December.

items.use: jubilar = pension someone off; jubilarse = retire. Regular. 'Estar jubilado' = be retired.
items.ex: Mi papá se jubiló a los sesenta y dos.
items.exEn: My dad retired at sixty-two.
items.latam: In Panama and other countries 'pensionarse' is also used.

items.use: enfermar = make someone sick; enfermarse = get sick. Regular.
items.ex: Me enfermé justo antes de las vacaciones.
items.exEn: I got sick right before vacation.
items.latam: Latin America says 'enfermarse'; Spain usually says 'ponerse enfermo' or 'enfermar'.

items.use: mejorar = improve something; mejorarse = recover. '¡Que te mejores!' = Get well soon (subjunctive).
items.ex: ¡Que te mejores pronto!
items.exEn: Get well soon!

items.use: acostumbrar a alguien = get someone used to; acostumbrarse a + noun/infinitive = get used to. Regular.
items.ex: Todavía no me acostumbro al calor de Panamá.
items.exEn: I still haven't gotten used to the Panama heat.

items.use: acercar = bring something closer; acercarse a = go up to. c→qu before e: me acerqué.
items.ex: No te acerques tanto al perro.
items.exEn: Don't get so close to the dog.

items.use: alejar = move something away; alejarse de = move away from, distance yourself. Regular.
items.ex: Aléjate de la orilla, hay olas grandes.
items.exEn: Move away from the edge, there are big waves.

items.use: mover = move something; moverse = move your body / get moving. o→ue: me muevo. For moving house use 'mudarse'.
items.ex: No te muevas, te voy a tomar una foto.
items.exEn: Don't move, I'm going to take your picture.

items.use: parar = stop something; pararse = stand up (Latin America) or come to a stop. Regular.
items.ex: Todos se pararon cuando entró el juez.
items.exEn: Everyone stood up when the judge came in.
items.latam: In Panama and most of Latin America 'pararse' means stand up. In Spain it only means stop; for stand up they say 'ponerse de pie' or 'levantarse'.

items.en: to get on/in (a vehicle), to climb on
items.use: subir = go up / raise; subirse a = get on a bus, into a car, onto something. Regular.
items.ex: Súbete al carro, que te llevo.
items.exEn: Get in the car, I'll give you a ride.

items.use: bajar = go down / lower; bajarse de = get out of a vehicle. Regular.
items.ex: Me bajo en la próxima parada.
items.exEn: I'm getting off at the next stop.

items.use: meter = put in; meterse en = go into (water, a place) or stick your nose into. Regular.
items.ex: No te metas en mis asuntos.
items.exEn: Stay out of my business.

items.en: to get out (of), to leave (a path or group)
items.use: salir = go out; salirse de = come out of something you're inside (the road, a group, the topic). Irregular: me salgo.
items.ex: El carro se salió de la carretera.
items.exEn: The car went off the road.

items.use: detener = arrest / stop someone; detenerse = come to a stop. Conjugated like tener: se detuvo.
items.ex: El bus se detuvo frente al hospital.
items.exEn: The bus stopped in front of the hospital.

items.en: to lie down; to burst out (+ a)
items.use: echar = throw / pour; echarse = lie down; echarse a + infinitive = burst out (echarse a reír, a llorar). Regular.
items.ex: Al oír el chiste, se echó a reír.
items.exEn: When he heard the joke, he burst out laughing.

items.use: estacionar = park a car; estacionarse = park (you + your car). Regular.
items.ex: Me estacioné frente al banco.
items.exEn: I parked in front of the bank.
items.latam: In Panama 'parquear(se)' is very common too. Spain says 'aparcar'.

items.use: dirigir = direct / manage; dirigirse a = head toward a place or speak to someone. g→j: me dirijo.
items.ex: Diríjase a la puerta 5, por favor.
items.exEn: Please proceed to gate 5.

items.use: Same as enojarse: enfadar = annoy someone; enfadarse con = get angry with. Regular. Good to recognize for the DELE.
items.ex: Mi jefe se enfada si llego tarde.
items.exEn: My boss gets angry if I arrive late.
items.latam: Mainly Spain. In Panama and Latin America say 'enojarse' or 'ponerse bravo'.

items.use: asustar = scare someone; asustarse = get scared. Regular.
items.ex: Me asusté cuando sonó el teléfono a medianoche.
items.exEn: I got scared when the phone rang at midnight.

items.use: sorprender = surprise someone; sorprenderse de = be surprised. '... de que' + subjunctive. Regular.
items.ex: Me sorprendí de lo barato que era.
items.exEn: I was surprised at how cheap it was.

items.en: to get upset; to bother (to do)
items.use: molestar = bother someone; molestarse = get annoyed, or take the trouble: 'no te molestes' = don't bother. Regular.
items.ex: No te molestes, yo lavo los platos.
items.exEn: Don't bother, I'll wash the dishes.

items.en: to get excited; to be moved
items.use: emocionar = move / thrill someone; emocionarse = get excited or emotional. Regular. Not 'excitarse' (sexual).
items.ex: Mi mamá se emocionó en mi graduación.
items.exEn: My mom got emotional at my graduation.

items.use: interesar = interest someone (Me interesa); interesarse por = show interest in. Regular.
items.ex: Se interesó por mi proyecto.
items.exEn: He showed interest in my project.

items.use: tranquilizar = calm someone; tranquilizarse = calm down. z→c before e: me tranquilicé.
items.ex: Tranquilízate, ya llegó la ambulancia.
items.exEn: Calm down, the ambulance is here.

items.use: decidir = decide; decidirse = finally make up your mind after doubting; decidirse a + infinitive. Regular.
items.ex: Por fin me decidí a aprender a manejar.
items.exEn: I finally made up my mind to learn to drive.

items.en: to feel like; to get up the courage (to)
items.use: animar = cheer up / encourage; animarse a = decide to / be up for. '¿Te animas?' = Are you up for it? Regular.
items.ex: ¿Te animas a ir a la playa mañana?
items.exEn: Are you up for going to the beach tomorrow?

items.en: to be in charge (of), to take care (of)
items.use: encargar = order (food, goods); encargarse de = handle / take care of. g→gu before e: me encargué.
items.ex: Yo me encargo de las bebidas.
items.exEn: I'll take care of the drinks.

items.use: aprovechar = make good use of (positive); aprovecharse de = take unfair advantage of (negative). Regular.
items.ex: Se aprovechó de su confianza.
items.exEn: He took advantage of her trust.

items.use: preguntar = ask someone; preguntarse = ask yourself / wonder. Regular.
items.ex: Me pregunto si va a llover hoy.
items.exEn: I wonder if it's going to rain today.

items.en: to think one is; to fall for
items.use: creer = believe; creerse = think you are (often arrogant) or fully believe a story. Irregular: se creyó.
items.ex: Se cree el más inteligente de la oficina.
items.exEn: He thinks he's the smartest in the office.

items.use: Like comerse: with a specific amount, it means drink it all. Regular.
items.ex: Se bebió dos vasos de agua seguidos.
items.exEn: He drank two glasses of water in a row.
items.latam: In Latin America 'tomarse' is more common than 'beberse'.

items.use: leer = read; leerse = read something from start to finish. Irregular: se leyó.
items.ex: Me leí el libro en un fin de semana.
items.exEn: I read the whole book in a weekend.

items.use: saber = know; saberse = know something completely (a song, a lesson). Irregular: me sé.
items.ex: Mi hijo se sabe todas las capitales.
items.exEn: My son knows all the capitals by heart.

items.en: to make an effort, to try hard
items.use: Almost always with se. 'esforzarse por/en' + infinitive. o→ue and z→c: me esfuerzo, me esforcé.
items.ex: Me esfuerzo mucho para mejorar mi español.
items.exEn: I try hard to improve my Spanish.

items.use: rendir = perform / last; rendirse = give up. e→i: me rindo, se rindió.
items.ex: No te rindas, ya casi terminas.
items.exEn: Don't give up, you're almost done.

items.use: Fixed expression; 'vencido' agrees with the subject: ella se da por vencida. 'dar' is irregular: me di.
items.ex: Después de tres intentos, se dio por vencida.
items.exEn: After three tries, she gave up.

items.en: to get confused, to get mixed up
items.use: confundir = confuse / mix up; confundirse = get it wrong; confundirse de = get the wrong (bus, day). Regular.
items.ex: Me confundí de bus y llegué tarde.
items.exEn: I took the wrong bus and arrived late.

items.use: lastimar = hurt someone; lastimarse = get hurt. Use the article: me lastimé la rodilla. Regular.
items.ex: Me lastimé la rodilla jugando fútbol.
items.exEn: I hurt my knee playing soccer.
items.latam: Common in Latin America; Spain prefers 'hacerse daño'.

items.en: to burn oneself; to get sunburned
items.use: quemar = burn something; quemarse = get burned. Use the article: me quemé la mano. Regular.
items.ex: Me quemé en la playa por no usar bloqueador.
items.exEn: I got sunburned at the beach for not using sunscreen.

items.use: resfriar = cool down; resfriarse = catch a cold. Accent: me resfrío. 'Estar resfriado' = have a cold.
items.ex: Me resfrié con el aire acondicionado.
items.exEn: I caught a cold from the air conditioning.
items.latam: In Panama you'll also hear 'agriparse' or 'me dio gripe'.

items.en: to get dizzy; to get carsick/seasick
items.use: marear = make someone dizzy (also: confuse with talk); marearse = feel dizzy or sick from motion. Regular.
items.ex: Me mareo cuando viajo en lancha.
items.exEn: I get seasick when I travel by boat.

items.use: recuperar = get something back; recuperarse de = recover from illness or a shock. Regular.
items.ex: Ya se recuperó de la operación.
items.exEn: He has recovered from the operation.

items.use: descomponer = break down / decompose; descomponerse = stop working. Often accidental: se me descompuso. Irregular like poner.
items.ex: Se me descompuso el carro en la autopista.
items.exEn: My car broke down on the highway.
items.latam: In Panama 'dañarse' is very common: 'se dañó la nevera'. Spain says 'estropearse' or 'averiarse'.

items.use: ensuciar = make something dirty; ensuciarse = get yourself dirty. Regular.
items.ex: Los niños se ensuciaron jugando en el lodo.
items.exEn: The kids got dirty playing in the mud.

items.en: to get cold, to cool down
items.use: enfriar = cool something; enfriarse = get cold. Accent: se enfría.
items.ex: Come ya, que se te enfría la sopa.
items.exEn: Eat now, or your soup will get cold.

items.use: referir = tell, refer (formal); referirse a = mean / talk about. e→ie and e→i: me refiero, se refirió.
items.ex: ¿A qué te refieres exactamente?
items.exEn: What exactly do you mean?

items.use: deshacer = undo, unpack; deshacerse de = get rid of. Conjugated like hacer: me deshice.
items.ex: Me deshice de toda la ropa vieja.
items.exEn: I got rid of all my old clothes.

items.en: to pretend to be, to act
items.use: hacerse el + adjective = pretend: hacerse el dormido, hacerse la loca. Article agrees with the person.
items.ex: No te hagas el tonto, sabes de qué hablo.
items.exEn: Don't play dumb, you know what I'm talking about.

items.use: Fixed expression, usually with a plural subject: nos pusimos de acuerdo. Irregular like poner.
items.ex: Al final nos pusimos de acuerdo con el precio.
items.exEn: In the end we agreed on the price.

items.use: Informal idiom (literally 'put your batteries in'): get serious, work harder. Irregular like poner.
items.ex: Si quieres pasar el examen, ponte las pilas.
items.exEn: If you want to pass the exam, get your act together.
items.latam: Very common in Panama and across Latin America.

items.use: empeñar = pawn; empeñarse en = insist stubbornly on. Regular.
items.ex: Se empeñó en pagar la cuenta.
items.exEn: He insisted on paying the bill.

items.use: hartar = annoy / stuff someone; hartarse de = get fed up with. 'Estar harto de' = be fed up. Regular.
items.ex: Me harté de esperar y me fui.
items.exEn: I got fed up with waiting and left.

items.use: o→ue with ü: me avergüenzo; z→c: me avergoncé. Formal; in speech people say 'me da vergüenza' or 'me da pena'.
items.ex: No me avergüenzo de mis errores.
items.exEn: I'm not ashamed of my mistakes.
items.latam: In Panama and much of Latin America 'me da pena' = I'm embarrassed (not 'I feel sorry').

items.use: inscribir = register someone; inscribirse en = sign up. Irregular participle: inscrito.
items.ex: Me inscribí en un curso de español.
items.exEn: I signed up for a Spanish course.

items.use: esconder = hide something; esconderse = hide yourself. Regular.
items.ex: El gato se escondió debajo de la cama.
items.exEn: The cat hid under the bed.

items.use: Only exists with se. Formal; in speech people say 'presumir de' or 'echárselas de'. Regular.
items.ex: Se jacta de no haber faltado nunca al trabajo.
items.exEn: He boasts that he has never missed work.

items.use: Formal synonym of darse cuenta de; always with se and 'de'. Regular.
items.ex: Nadie se percató de su ausencia.
items.exEn: Nobody noticed he was missing.

items.use: Almost always with se and 'de'. Used for taking control of things or feelings. Regular.
items.ex: El miedo se apoderó de todos.
items.exEn: Fear took hold of everyone.
